Hello everyone! I've just done something awfully exciting this afternoon - made sunflower seed butter! I was hesitant to try this after a failed attempt to make homemade peanut butter years ago. But today I was motivated by a serious craving for something gooey and tasty, and so the experimentation began!

I'd like to mention that this recipe is oil and sugar free since I personally like to avoid added oils and refined sweeteners as much as possible. I chose sunflower seeds because they're the cheapest nut/seed out there (bought 1lb for $3.60 vs almonds which run upwards of $14/lb!) and because I'm not the biggest peanut fan. Of course, you could substitute any nut of your choice and still follow this recipe!

Ingredients: - 3 cups raw sunflower seeds (or substitute peanuts, almonds, walnuts, whatever you like) - 1 tbsp cinnamon (this is specifically because I used sunflower seeds which have a slight bitterness. The cinnamon adds sweetness without any sugar. Skip if you'd like) - 1/4 - 1/2 tsp salt - Food processor with a high setting

First toast your seeds at 360 degrees F on an ungreased tray. This step is crucial because the toasting will release natural oils and make blending easier. If you don't toast them (like I did during my peanut butter catastrophe) you'll end up with a crumbly lumpy texture that will never turn smooth.

Toast for about 2 - 3 minutes at a time, tossing them with a spatula between intervals. The whole toasting process should take around 10 minutes (look for that golden brown color and aroma - no burnt bits!)

Once toasted, take out your seeds and immediately transfer them to your food processor, you want them hot to continue releasing oils. Let them whirl on the high setting for a few minutes and occasionally scrape down the sides to keep every moving. This step takes PATIENTS! I have a not-so-great Cuisinart food processor and the whole blending/scraping procedure took well over 20 minutes. The better your fp the less time and effort. In about 15-25 minutes, you'll start seeing that iconic buttery texture! Add your cinnamon and salt at this point and continue blending until you're satisfied with the creaminess.

Convert your nut butter into an open jar and let it sit on your counter until completely cooled ( it will still be hot! Don't put a lid over your jar, the steam will mix with the oils and encourage it to spoil).

Seal with a lid and place in the fridge. Should stay good for around a month (if it even lasts that long in your hungry household). You should end up with about 18 tbsp of nut butter - not bad considering it's low in cost, has no additives or preservatives, is refined sugar and oil free, and was a totally liberating experience to make (for me anyways)!

~EggHead
